reference_answer.response: Your own sofa fits the stated personal-property scope for this fire, subject to the policy terms. The built-in cabinets are part of the landlord’s building and do not belong under your personal-property coverage. You have not described a liability allegation, so I would not invent one or promise that liability coverage pays for the cabinets from the repair estimate. This is not a claim approval.

checks.rationale: The sofa is owned by the named insured and damaged by fire within the policy interval.
The cabinets belong to the landlord’s building.
The customer explicitly says there is no allegation or demand.
The two ownership categories are explicit.

rubric.criterion: Separately classifies the named insured’s sofa and the landlord’s built-in cabinets instead of treating all fire damage alike.
Does not invent fault or a liability claim/payment route from the repair estimate where the customer expressly reports no allegation.

failure_modes: Treating built-in building fixtures as the tenant’s personal property
Inventing a liability allegation to cover building repairs
rationale: Sofa in, cabinets out. Repair estimate is not a liability allegation. Informational answer only.
